The feeder identifier is a geographic/infrastructure identifier that pinpoints a specific distribution area. In energy data, feeder numbers can be cross-referenced with utility records to identify specific consumers or small groups of consumers, especially in areas with limited housing units (70 in this case). This constitutes location data that can be used for tracking individuals.

The substation identifier, combined with the feeder number, narrows down the geographic location to a very specific area. This combination can be used to identify the physical location of consumers, constituting location data that enables tracking of individuals or small groups.

The date column represents temporal information for aggregate measurements. While dates can be used in combination with other data to track patterns over time, the date itself in an aggregate energy dataset is not directly personal data. It is standard metadata for time-series data and does not by itself identify an individual.

The housing units count is aggregate demographic data representing the number of residential units in a feeder area. While a small count (70) could theoretically aid re-identification when combined with other data, the count itself is a statistical aggregate and does not directly identify any individual. It falls under demographic characteristics at an area level.

The industry and commerce count is aggregate data representing the number of commercial units in the area. While a small number (11) could narrow down identification when combined with specific consumption data (e.g., g4_shop_hairdresser, g5_bakery), the count alone is a statistical aggregate and does not directly identify specific businesses or individuals.

The storage heaters power capacity is technical infrastructure data describing the aggregate installed capacity in the feeder area. It does not directly identify any individual consumer. The public lighting power capacity is technical infrastructure data for public infrastructure. It does not relate to any individual consumer and is a public utility characteristic of the area. This is the least sensitive column in the dataset.

It represents service consumption behaviour at an area level.

The continuous energy consumption is aggregate data for 24/7 loads in the feeder area. It represents baseline consumption that does not vary significantly by time of day. The aggregate value does not directly identify specific consumers or their personal data.
